title: Students protest school conditions and teacher shortages in Créteil

tea.why: Students protested against deteriorating school facilities, teacher shortages, and poor infrastructure.
tea.want: Better school facilities, sufficient teaching staff, and proper learning conditions.
tea.changed: Sep 15: Initial student demonstrations began in Créteil over deteriorating school facilities and teacher shortages.

summary: In mid-September, students in Créteil, near Paris, initiated demonstrations over deteriorating school infrastructure and teacher shortages. Protesters highlighted issues such as leaking roofs, collapsed ceilings, broken furniture, and rat-infested classrooms, particularly in lower-income neighbourhoods. The movement aimed to secure sufficient staff and suitable facilities for proper education. As the demonstrations grew, they spread to other Paris suburbs and nationwide, drawing workers, trade unions, and political groups, alongside subsequent class strikes and school blockades. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence as clashes with police intensified, with officers deploying tear gas, batons, and crowd-control weapons.
demands: Fix infrastructure issues such as leaking roofs and collapsed ceilings
response: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence as unrest grew, while police deployed tear gas, batons, and other crowd-control weapons to disperse demonstrators during confrontations.

updates.text: Students in Créteil began demonstrating over teacher shortages and deteriorating school facilities.
